1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. The pairs the exam likes to confuse. The lists to know by heart. Technique for each question style. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All learning outcomes. Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse
1.text: The pairs the exam likes to confuse. Output or outcome or benefit. delivered product or result of change or measurable gain. Risk or issue. might happen or has happened. Appetite or tolerance (risk). willingness to take risk or limit of acceptable exposure. Tolerance or exception. permitted deviation or tolerance forecast to be exceeded. Checkpoint or highlight report. team manager to project manager or project manager to board. Project board or project manager. accountable, decides or manages day to day. Quality control or assurance. checks the product or independently checks the system. P I D or project log. baseline decided at the start or records updated all the time.

1.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: The pairs the exam likes to confuse. Leadership or management. inspire people or plan and control work. Project plan or stage plan or exception plan. whole project or one stage or replaces a plan when tolerance is exceeded. Starting up or initiating. is it worthwhile? (brief) or solid foundations (P I D). Stage boundary or closing. end of a stage except the last or end of the project.

1.title: The pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: The pairs the exam likes to confuse. The figure shows this: Map of the whole course: five elements, seven principles, seven practices, seven processes.

1.title: The lists to know by heart
1.text: The lists to know by heart. Five integrated elements. principles, people, practices, processes, project context. Seven principles. continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project. Seven practices. business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress. Seven processes. starting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary, closing a project. Seven aspects of performance. benefits, risks, quality, scope, cost, time, sustainability. Three project interests. business, user, supplier. Project board. Executive, Senior User(s), Senior Supplier(s). Business case lifecycle. develop, verify, maintain, confirm.

1.title: Technique for each question style
1.text: Technique for each question style. Standard. Read the last line, name the term, eliminate. Missing word. Read the sentence with each option; choose the definition. List. Mark each statement true or false; pick the pair. Negative. Rewrite as "find the false one"; check each option. Old wording alert: themes, six aspects, and the fifty-five percent pass mark belong to the older edition. In prince two seven they are practices, seven aspects and sixty percent. Exam tip: Before you answer, ask: which of the five elements is this about? Then match the term to its element (for example, tolerances belong to progress and plans, roles to organizing). Exam tip: With no negative marking, answer every question; flag hard ones and return with the time left.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which list names the seven prince two processes? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Starting up, directing, initiating, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary, closing a project. B is the practices and C the elements.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A supplier might be late. Which term fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Risk. It might happen, so it is a risk.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) The project board is accountable for the project's success. (two) The project manager is accountable for the business case. (three) A checkpoint report goes from the team manager to the project manager. (four) The risk register is part of the P I D. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and three. Statements one and three are correct.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word. blank is the permissible deviation from a plan's target before escalation. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Tolerance. That is a tolerance.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which principle does a project breach if its board never rechecks the business case? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Ensure continued business justification. The justification must remain valid.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which report goes from the project manager to the board at regular intervals? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Highlight report. The highlight report is time-driven and goes to the board.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which activity checks products against their criteria? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Quality control. Control checks the products.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. How many marks are needed to pass? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: thirty-six. The pass mark is thirty-six of sixty.

1.title: Practice Question 9
1.text: Question nine. Which process confirms acceptance of the project product? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Closing a project. Closing a project confirms acceptance.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the pass mark? Answer: thirty-six of sixty (sixty percent). Question two. Which learning outcome has the highest weight? Answer: The practices, at sixty percent. Question three. Name the seven principles. Answer: Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the seven practices. Answer: Business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress. Question five. What did prince two six call the practices? Answer: Themes. Question six. Which aspect of project performance was added in prince two seven? Answer: Sustainability.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: sixty questions, sixty minutes, thirty-six to pass, no negative marking. Weights: key concepts three, principles eight, people fourteen, practices sixty, processes fifteen. Method: keyword, name the term, eliminate, choose the definition. Old wording: themes, six aspects, fifty-five percent pass mark. Always: answer every question. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
